name: Jake Williamson
who: British men's open doubles world-record holder (47:57 with Fabi Eisenlauer, Berlin 2025); Puma-sponsored, part of Instagram's Athletes for Purpose roster.
why: Follow for the record-breaking doubles racing and for an openly gay athlete pushing HYROX toward a wider, more inclusive audience.
takeaway: Find a doubles partner whose pace matches yours exactly — mismatched pairs lose time.

name: Fabian Eisenlauer
who: German HYROX Elite athlete and running coach; set the men's open doubles world record with Jake Williamson in 2025 and holds one of the fastest men's open times ever.
why: Follow for a genuine ex-smoker-to-elite transformation story and running-coach breakdowns that double as real training content.
takeaway: Build your running volume up gradually from a low baseline toward elite pace.

name: Jonathon Wynn
who: Australian HYROX Elite athlete and ex-Special Forces commando; part of Australia's back-to-back Mixed Relay World Championship-winning team (2025, 2026).
why: Follow for a rare sobriety-and-military-to-elite-racing story alongside genuine championship relay credentials.
takeaway: Use structured, disciplined daily habits as the backbone of your race prep.

name: Harry Thompson
who: English HYROX Elite athlete; 2025 Men's Pro World Champion (all age groups, Chicago) and member of England's bronze-medal 2026 Mixed Relay team.
why: Follow for an honest, no-filter look at life as a world champion who left corporate law to race and coach full-time.
takeaway: Be honest and transparent about your process, not just the highlight-reel wins.

name: Katherine Fahsbender
who: American HYROX Pro racer who went from casual runner to Pro Women's winner (Atlanta) and Pro Doubles winner (Houston) in about 18 months.
why: Follow to watch one of the sport's fastest-rising talents in real time as she pushes toward Elite 15 contention.
takeaway: Go from casual runner to competitive racer by committing fully for a defined stretch.

name: Rebecca Mason
who: Britain's most successful female HYROX racer historically; 2022 age-group World Champion and Elite 15 competitor 2022-2024, now a full-time HYROX 1-1 coach.
why: Follow for coaching grounded in real Elite 15 experience, from a former elite gymnast who built her own path in the sport.
takeaway: Draw on your background in another sport to inform technique, not just raw fitness.

name: Max Pineau
who: French HYROX Pro athlete and TikTok star (posts as "pinaliste"); races doubles and solo Pro divisions while building one of the sport's biggest short-form followings.
why: Follow for high-volume, high-energy running and HYROX content that pulls a huge general-fitness audience into the sport.
takeaway: Post high-volume, high-energy training content consistently — frequency builds an audience as much as quality.

name: Aoife O'Rourke
who: Two-time Olympic boxer and 2025 World Championship boxing silver medalist from Ireland; won a HYROX doubles age-group World title with sister Lisa in 2025.
why: Follow for the novelty of an Olympic-level combat-sport athlete crossing over into HYROX and bringing her boxing following with her.
takeaway: Bring combat-sport conditioning, like footwork and explosive power, into your Hyrox stations.

name: Gustav Cordua
who: Danish HYROX Elite 15 doubles athlete; Danish record holder who won Men's Pro Doubles at the 2026 Stockholm World Championships with Sebastian Ifversen.
why: Follow a fast-climbing Nordic racer breaking national records while balancing an engineering master's degree.
takeaway: Balance demanding academic or work commitments with structured elite training rather than choosing one.

name: Jack Driscoll
who: American HYROX Elite hopeful and full-time firefighter; sub-60 Pro Solo winner (Vancouver) chasing his first Elite 15 spot.
why: Follow for in-depth, reference-quality training breakdowns filmed with actual Elite 15 athletes, from a firefighter with a sub-5 mile and a 500lb squat.
takeaway: Balance a strong running base with heavy strength work rather than picking one over the other.

name: Isaac Sanderson
who: Canadian HYROX Pro athlete sponsored by LSKD and 1st Phorm; regular Pro-division racer across Canadian events.
why: Follow for an under-the-radar Canadian racer's-eye view of the Pro circuit and sponsor-backed training content.
takeaway: Race consistently across your regional circuit to build a sponsor-worthy track record over time.

name: Jannik Czapla
who: German HYROX Elite 15 athlete and HYROX Germany ambassador; part of Germany's silver-medal 2026 Mixed Relay team alongside Tim Wenisch and Linda Meier.
why: Follow a young German elite building a coaching brand alongside his own Elite 15 racing career.
takeaway: Build a coaching brand alongside your own racing career from early on, not after retiring.

name: Charlotte Haglund
who: Swedish HYROX Pro Women athlete who ranked 13th of 731 (top 1%) at the 2025 World Championships and raced on Sweden's 2026 Elite 15 and Mixed Relay teams.
why: Follow a quietly excellent Nordic racer whose results outpace her current profile.
takeaway: Let quiet, consistent top-tier finishes build your credibility even without a big following.

name: Lily Sharp
who: Australian HYROX Pro Doubles athlete with results across multiple seasons and partners (national top-3 rankings); active HYROX content creator.
why: Follow for a working Pro-division racer's view of the doubles circuit, from qualifiers through World Championships.
takeaway: Race with different doubles partners across seasons to learn what pairing style suits you best.
